problem.title: MongoDB Replica Set Secondary Out-of-Sync (Oplog Window Overrun)
problem.prompt: MongoDB primary undergoing heavy batch data import with a small default oplog size.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "MongoDB oplog retention must provide at least a 24- to 48-hour safety buffer against heavy batch ingestion surges."
Production Hardening: Configure oplogSizeMB generously (e.g. 50 GB to 100 GB) ensuring at least a 48-hour replication window, and monitor MongoDB replication lag metrics continuously.
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.

Failure Cascade Path: Scale Surge → Unbounded Contention → Physical Bottleneck → 💥 Outage Cascade

stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: Scale Surge → Unbounded Contention → Physical Bottleneck → 💥 Outage Cascade.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Primary writes generate oplog entries faster than the Secondary can replicate them. The Secondary falls behind past the earliest timestamp in the Primary's capped oplog collection, falling into RECOVERING / FATAL state and requiring a full resync.
Breakdown Chain: Scale Surge → Unbounded Contention → Physical Bottleneck → 💥 Outage Cascade
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.
